You are a visual scene extractor for an illustrated adventure gamebook pipeline. The source text may be in French; translate everything into English — no French word may remain anywhere except in "last_action_quote".

BOOK CONTEXT (use ONLY to determine genre, era, tone and setting style — NEVER as a source of characters, creatures, or objects for the scene):
"""
{CONTEXT}
"""

HERO VISIBILITY RULE:
{HERO_RULE}

Output ONLY a single valid JSON object. No markdown, no text before or after.

Structure (fields must appear in this exact order):
{
  "last_action_quote": "Copy, in the ORIGINAL language, the VERY LAST physical action or observation described in the text below — the closest possible sentence(s) to the end of the whole passage. Do not stop at an earlier action if the text continues afterward.",
  "scene": "A description of ONE frozen instant, English only, 1-2 sentences, based on last_action_quote above.",
  "environment": "2-4 word location label, English only, only if stated or clearly implied in the text below",
  "characters": ["people or sentient beings ONLY, no duplicates. If the text addresses the reader as 'you'/'vous', include an entry for them unless HERO VISIBILITY RULE says otherwise."],
  "creatures": ["monsters/animals ONLY, empty array if none explicitly named in the text below"],
  "objects": ["short concrete nouns, English only, maximum 4 items, only if literally mentioned in the text below"],
  "lighting": "short phrase, max 5 words, based only on light explicitly mentioned in the text below; write 'unspecified' if none",
  "action": "1-2 words maximum",
  "composition": "short phrase, max 8 words"
}

STRICT rules:
- Every character, creature, object and detail in your answer must come from the TEXT OF THE SECTION below, never from BOOK CONTEXT. BOOK CONTEXT only tells you the genre/setting style to match — it does not describe what is happening right now.
- Never invent proper names, weather, or scenery details not explicitly present in the text below.
- Never classify a person as an object or an object as a character.
- Every word must be in English, except "last_action_quote".
- Match the genre/era of BOOK CONTEXT exactly, but only describe elements from the text below.

Text of the section:
"""
{SECTION_TEXT}
"""

The hero/reader ("you"/"vous") MUST be clearly present and visible in this scene as the main character. Always include them explicitly in "characters" (e.g. "the adventurer"), even if the source text does not name them directly — if the text describes an action from their point of view, they are physically present and doing it. The scene description must show them as a clear, central figure taking part in the action, not just implied or off-screen.

CRITICAL: The hero/reader ("you"/"vous") must be COMPLETELY ABSENT from this scene. Do not include them in "characters" under any name (not "the adventurer", not "you", not "the hero", not any pronoun-based entry). Describe ONLY the environment, creatures, or objects visible — as if the scene were an empty room or landscape with no human figure present. If the source text only makes sense with someone acting, describe the RESULT of that action (the object, the door, the creature) rather than the act of a person doing it.

You are reviewing and correcting a JSON scene extraction for an illustrated adventure gamebook. The source text may be in French.

ORIGINAL SECTION TEXT:
"""
{SECTION_TEXT}
"""

BOOK CONTEXT:
"""
{CONTEXT}
"""

JSON TO REVIEW:
"""
{PREVIOUS_JSON}
"""

The JSON above contains a "_warnings" field listing issues to fix. For each warning:
- "empty_field_X" → fill field X based on the ORIGINAL SECTION TEXT, following the same rules as a normal extraction (concrete, visual, English only).
- "residual_non_english_characters" → translate any remaining non-English word to English (except inside "last_action_quote", which must stay in the original language).
- "too_many_objects_N" → keep only the 4 most explicitly stated objects, remove the rest.
- "no_characters" → add the reader/hero as a character (e.g. "the adventurer"), unless BOOK CONTEXT or the JSON indicates they must stay hidden.
- "last_action_quote_too_early_ratio_X" → the quoted moment is too early in the text (only X% of the way through). Re-read the ORIGINAL SECTION TEXT and find a LATER action or observation, closer to the end, then update "last_action_quote" and rewrite "scene" accordingly.
- "invalid_json" or "no_json_found" → re-extract the scene entirely from the ORIGINAL SECTION TEXT, following the same structure.
- Any other warning not listed above → use your best judgment based on the ORIGINAL SECTION TEXT to fix it.

Do not change any field that has no related warning — copy it exactly as-is.

Output ONLY the corrected JSON object, same structure and field order, WITHOUT the "_warnings" field (remove it entirely). No markdown, no text before or after.

import json

data = json.loads(arg0)

STYLE_GLOBAL = """Traditional hand-drawn fantasy adventure illustration.
Black and white ink illustration.
Detailed pen linework.
Cross-hatching for shadows.
Slightly rough traditional paper texture.
Dark medieval fantasy.
Consistent printed-book illustration aesthetic."""

UNIVERS_GLOBAL = """Dark medieval fantasy world.
Ancient underground environments.
Realistic medieval architecture and objects.
Dark and mysterious atmosphere.
No modern elements."""

CONTEXTE_LOCAL = """The current story location is an underground cave system.
Wet dark rock walls.
The main light sources are lanterns and torches.
No sky and no natural daylight."""

characters = ", ".join(data.get("characters", [])) or "no characters"
creatures = ", ".join(data.get("creatures", []))
objects = ", ".join(data.get("objects", []))

scene_line = data.get("scene", "")

details = []
if creatures:
    details.append(f"Creatures present: {creatures}.")
if objects:
    details.append(f"Visible objects: {objects}.")
if data.get("lighting"):
    details.append(f"Lighting: {data['lighting']}.")
if data.get("composition"):
    details.append(f"Composition: {data['composition']}.")

scene_block = scene_line + " " + " ".join(details)

result = f"{STYLE_GLOBAL}\n\n{UNIVERS_GLOBAL}\n\n{CONTEXTE_LOCAL}\n\n{scene_block}"
